prompt: Which of these stays Quitanda's job after the orders move to Cloud SQL?
hint: The table splits the work in two columns.

choices.text: Taking the daily backup
choices.why: Automated backups are Cloud SQL's.

choices.text: Adding the index a slow report needs
choices.why: Right. Indexes, queries and schema stay with whoever wrote them.

choices.text: Replacing a disk that failed
choices.why: The hardware is Google's.

choices.text: Applying the operating system's security patches
choices.why: That is in Cloud SQL's column.

prompt: On Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL, what is the `postgres` user the instance is created with?
hint: Look at the role it belongs to, and at what that role is not.

choices.text: The operating system's user, with a shell
choices.why: There is no shell on the machine.

choices.text: A true PostgreSQL superuser, as on any server
choices.why: Google's documentation says it is not.

choices.text: A `cloudsqlsuperuser` member, not a superuser
choices.why: Right. It can create databases and roles, and cannot run `ALTER SYSTEM`.

choices.text: A read-only user until a flag is set
choices.why: It can create and write; it cannot reconfigure the server.

prompt: A report's query reads the whole `orders` table every minute and the CPU sits at 95%. Someone proposes a bigger instance. What does the lesson's line say about it?
hint: Which risk moved to Google and which did not.

choices.text: It is the right fix, since capacity is Google's problem now
choices.why: Capacity is bought, not managed; the query is still yours.

choices.text: It hides a design problem at a price; the index is still Quitanda's to add
choices.why: Right. Managed moves the operational risk, not the design risk.

choices.text: Cloud SQL would have added the index on its own
choices.why: No provider adds your indexes.

choices.text: The maintenance window will fix it on the next restart
choices.why: A restart changes nothing about a query.

prompt: `gcloud sql instances create orders --region=southamerica-east1 …` is run with no `--database-version`. What engine does the instance get?
hint: The reference prints the default beside the flag.

choices.text: Whichever engine the project used last
choices.why: The default is fixed in the command, not remembered.

choices.text: None; the command refuses to run without it
choices.why: It runs, and creates MySQL.

choices.text: PostgreSQL, the most common choice
choices.why: The reference says otherwise.

choices.text: MySQL 8.0
choices.why: Right. The default is `MYSQL_8_0`.

prompt: A company already owns SQL Server licences. On Cloud SQL, what happens to them?
hint: There is a note on the pricing page.

choices.text: Unusable: the licence is in the hourly price
choices.why: Right. The pricing page says Cloud SQL does not support BYOL.

choices.text: They cover high availability, which otherwise needs two
choices.why: A highly available instance pays for one licence anyway.

choices.text: They replace the Enterprise Plus edition charge
choices.why: The edition and the licence are separate lines.

choices.text: They are applied, and the hourly price drops
choices.why: Cloud SQL does not support bring-your-own-licence.

prompt: Why does `--cpu=2 --memory=8GiB` fail on an Enterprise Plus instance?
hint: Read the `--tier` reference.

choices.text: Enterprise Plus has no 2 vCPU machines
choices.why: `db-perf-optimized-N-2` is 2 vCPU.

choices.text: Its machines are names, given with `--tier`
choices.why: Right. Enterprise takes numbers; Enterprise Plus takes a name.

choices.text: Memory must be given in MiB on Enterprise Plus
choices.why: The unit is not the problem.

choices.text: The flags only work with MySQL
choices.why: They work on Enterprise for every engine.

prompt: Match each property to the edition it belongs to, as the lesson's table gives them.
hint: One right-hand value belongs to neither.

pairs.left: Up to 35 days of transaction logs

prompt: `--backup-start-time=03:00` is written meaning the quiet hour in São Paulo. When does the backup start?
hint: The reference names the time zone.

choices.text: Whenever the maintenance window falls
choices.why: Backups and maintenance have separate times.

choices.text: At 03:00 in the laptop's time zone
choices.why: The instance never sees the laptop's zone.

choices.text: 03:00 in São Paulo, the region's time
choices.why: The flag does not read the region's zone.

choices.text: 03:00 UTC, which is midnight in São Paulo
choices.why: Right. The time is in UTC; 06:00 is what was meant.

prompt: Why does the lesson's command carry no `--root-password`?
hint: Think of where a password on a command line ends up.

choices.text: It would sit in shell history and `ps`
choices.why: Right. It is set afterwards with `--prompt-for-password`, or replaced by IAM.

choices.text: PostgreSQL instances on Cloud SQL have no password
choices.why: The `postgres` user has one once it is set.

choices.text: The flag exists only for SQL Server
choices.why: It exists for every engine.

choices.text: Cloud SQL generates one and e-mails it to the owner
choices.why: Nothing is e-mailed; the password is set afterwards.

prompt: An instance has only a private address. A developer on a laptop at home needs to run a query on it. Which path fits what the lesson describes?
hint: The private address has no route from the internet.

choices.text: Turn on `--storage-auto-increase`
choices.why: That is about the disk.

choices.text: Add the laptop's public address to the authorised networks
choices.why: Authorised networks apply to a public IP, which this instance has none of.

choices.text: The Auth Proxy, run from inside the VPC
choices.why: Right. The private address is reached only from inside the network.

choices.text: Connect to the connection name directly with `psql`
choices.why: A connection name is for the proxy and the connectors, not an address.

prompt: The Cloud SQL Auth Proxy names an instance by its connection ___, which reads `planner-dev:southamerica-east1:quitanda-orders`.
hint: Project, region and instance, joined by colons.

prompt: After `ALTER SYSTEM SET max_connections = 400` and a reload, `SHOW max_connections` printed 100. Why?
hint: Look at its context in `pg_settings`.

choices.text: 400 is above the limit for a laptop
choices.why: After the restart it was 400.

choices.text: `ALTER SYSTEM` only works for logging settings
choices.why: It wrote both into `postgresql.auto.conf`.

choices.text: The reload failed
choices.why: It returned `t`, and the other setting was applied.

choices.text: A `postmaster` setting, read at start only
choices.why: Right. `pending_restart` was `t` until the restart.

prompt: On Cloud SQL, setting which of these flags restarts the instance?
hint: The rule is PostgreSQL's context column.

choices.text: `work_mem`
choices.why: It is `user`; even a session can change it.

choices.text: `shared_buffers`
choices.why: Right. It is `postmaster`, laid out at start.

choices.text: None; Cloud SQL applies every flag live
choices.why: Flags in the `postmaster` context need a restart there too.

choices.text: `log_min_duration_statement`
choices.why: It is `superuser`; a reload applies it.

prompt: An instance was created with `--database-flags=log_min_duration_statement=500`. Later someone runs `gcloud sql instances patch quitanda-orders --database-flags=max_connections=400`. What flags does it have afterwards?
hint: The documentation warns about what the flag does to the list.

choices.text: Both, since a patch only adds
choices.why: A patch with `--database-flags` replaces the list.

choices.text: Only `max_connections=400`
choices.why: Right. Every patch has to name every flag it wants to keep.

choices.text: Only `log_min_duration_statement=500`, since a restart flag is refused
choices.why: It is accepted, with a restart.

choices.text: None, as with `--clear-database-flags`
choices.why: Clearing is a different flag.

prompt: A nightly report needs 64MB for its sorts, and the default `work_mem` is 4MB. What is the cheapest change, on the laptop or on Cloud SQL?
hint: `work_mem` is a `user` setting.

choices.text: Grant the report's role `SUPERUSER`
choices.why: Cloud SQL gives nobody that, and `SET` does not need it.

choices.text: Raise the flag for the whole instance, and restart
choices.why: It needs no restart, and every connection would get 64MB.

choices.text: `SET work_mem = '64MB'` in the report's own session
choices.why: Right. One query changes and nothing restarts.

choices.text: Move the report to Enterprise Plus
choices.why: The edition does not set `work_mem`.

prompt: At 0.062 USD per vCPU-hour and 0.0105 USD per GiB-hour, what does an Enterprise instance of 4 vCPU and 16 GiB cost for its machine in a month of 730 hours, in USD?
hint: Four of one, sixteen of the other, then 730 hours.

prompt: A SQL Server Standard instance has 2 vCPU. For how many cores is the licence charged?
hint: Microsoft's rule is on the pricing page.

choices.text: 4, the minimum per instance
choices.why: Right. Fewer than four vCPU are charged as four.

choices.text: 1, since the licence is per instance
choices.why: It is per core.

choices.text: 8, two per vCPU for hyper-threading
choices.why: Threads per core change the vCPU count, not a multiplier on it.

choices.text: 2, one per vCPU
choices.why: There is a minimum.

prompt: Order the five instances of `sqlcost.py` by their month, most expensive first.
hint: The licence, then the standby, then the edition.

prompt: Quitanda's Enterprise instance is two years past the end of standard support for its PostgreSQL version. What is the most direct way to bring its bill down?
hint: Read the extended support line again.

choices.text: Turn high availability off
choices.why: It is zonal already; and the charge is per vCPU for the old version.

choices.text: Upgrade the major version, which Cloud SQL does not do for you
choices.why: Right. The extended support charge stops with the upgrade.

choices.text: Stop it with `--activation-policy=never` at night
choices.why: That saves hours of everything; the extra charge stays while it runs.

choices.text: Move it to Enterprise Plus
choices.why: Extended support applies to the version, whatever the edition.

prompt: Which of these keep billing while an instance is stopped with `--activation-policy=never`? Choose all that apply.
hint: Only the machine stops.

choices.text: The SSD disk
choices.why: Yes: storage is billed by what is set.

choices.text: The backups
choices.why: Yes: they are billed by what they hold.

choices.text: The vCPUs and the memory
choices.why: Those are the charge that stops.

choices.text: A reserved public address
choices.why: Yes: an address not in use is billed by the hour.
